rounds.proof_sketch: The mutated variable ROW_TILES is declared on line 18 but never used anywhere in the kernel. Searching the entire kernel: (1) tile loop uses 'for (int tile = blockRow; tile <= blockCol; tile++)' - no ROW_TILES, (2) grid dimensions computed in host code use '(N + TILE_SIZE - 1) / TILE_SIZE' directly, not ROW_TILES, (3) block indices come from blockIdx.x/y. ROW_TILES is dead code.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the value of ROW_TILES from (N + TILE_SIZE - 1) / TILE_SIZE to (N + TILE_SIZE - 1) / TILE_SIZE - 1, but ROW_TILES is never read or referenced anywhere else in the kernel code. It's a dead variable - computed but never consumed. The grid launch dimensions are computed separately in the host code using the original formula. The tile iteration loop uses blockRow and blockCol directly, which come from blockIdx, not from ROW_TILES. Since the mutated variable has no dataflow to any computation, memory access, or control flow decision, the mutation has zero semantic effect regardless of input values.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is truly unkillable under any value-level testing because ROW_TILES is dead code. The only way to expose this mutation would be to modify the kernel to actually use ROW_TILES, which is not a valid testing approach. No input tensor values can affect whether a dead variable's value matters.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing frameworks should include dead code detection as a pre-filter to avoid generating mutations on unused variables. Static analysis to identify variables that are defined but never read would eliminate this class of equivalent mutants before expensive dynamic testing.
